environment.tool: manual audit of the tag source + live compiled binary; scripted peer emitting exact response bytes, hexdump of client output

findings.description: The 1xx branch loops back to parse a second head, but respleft from the interim head is left live; when the real 200 arrives its body is emitted only up to the interim length, and the interim head is stamped with that same Content-Length. An upstream that sends 100 with Content-Length: 100 replaces the client's HELLO with whatever bytes follow, and the client sees a Content-Length that does not describe its body. Precondition: an attacker-influenced upstream and a proxied location.
findings.title: An interim head's Content-Length is applied to the real response body, so the upstream chooses the bytes the client receives

findings.description: The loop continues as soon as a head parses and never consumes bytes belonging to the interim response, so any interim that carries a body desynchronises the parse and the client gets 502. Concretely 101 with Upgrade, 100 followed by body bytes, and nine consecutive interims were each 502 on this build. Precondition: an attacker-influenced upstream.
findings.title: The interim loop never skips an interim body, so 101, a 100 carrying a body, and a ninth interim are all 502

limitations: All RCE is on the upstream host
methods: Read the release source from the tag

Captured client bytes as hex and diffed against the control
Sent a follow-up request on the same connection
